correctness.rationale: Exact monomial coefficient follows from factorial differentiation and integration with normalized Fock basis. Products are one fixed weighted shift; logarithmic finite-product expansions yield \(E_2=h_1h_2(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)\) and, upon resonance, \(E_3=-h_1h_2(h_1^2-h_2^2)/2\). Distinctness makes the relevant coefficient nonzero. Rearrangement of a regularly varying weight sequence produces \(s_n\sim Cn^{-r}\), the sharp Schatten criterion and logarithmic endpoint. The standalone checker verifies thousands of finite exact identities and numeric limits but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 Fock–Sobolev theory identifies critical integral operators only up to compact perturbation; quantifying their nonzero compact commutators is a natural next operator-ideal question. Arithmetic equality of the first drift indices forces an otherwise hidden full power of additional smoothing, giving two distinct exact singular asymptotic coefficients and sharp weak-Schatten boundaries across an infinite natural family. This is structural and parameter-complete within the family, not a sole finite example or arbitrary cutoff.
